sample_unit: radiation oncology vignettes (plus 300 TXIT multiple-choice items)

links.outcome: GPT-5 accuracy on exam benchmark versus real-world vignette correctness ratings
links.effect: TXIT accuracy 92.8% (GPT-4 78.8%, GPT-3.5 62.1%); vignette correctness mean 3.24/4, with errors clustering in complex scenarios requiring precise trial knowledge or clinical adaptation.
links.quote: Errors clustered in complex scenarios requiring precise trial knowledge or detailed clinical adaptation.

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement among four radiation oncologists rating AI outputs
links.effect: Inter-rater agreement was low (Fleiss' κ 0.083 for correctness), reflecting inherent variability in clinical judgment.
links.quote: Inter-rater agreement was low (Fleiss' κ 0.083 for correctness), reflecting inherent variability in clinical judgment.

links.outcome: Hallucinations and clinical knowledge errors in GPT-5 radiation oncology treatment plans
links.effect: Hallucinations flagged in 10.0% of individual reviewer assessments (24 of 240); no case reached majority consensus; substantive errors persisted, clustered in complex scenarios needing precise trial knowledge.
links.quote: Hallucinations were rare, flagged in 10.0% of all individual reviewer assessments (24 of 240), and no patient case reached majority consensus for their presence.

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic and treatment recommendation performance of GPT-5 using an examination benchmark and clinical vignettes rated by oncologists, noting the need for expert oversight but not testing a specific deployment safeguard intervention.
